# Export scope

The exported object is the focused Part 2 K562 cohort used for perturbation analysis and classification. It is distinct from the broad Part 1 coverage subset. The export maps normalized expression to `X`, raw counts to the `counts` layer, and includes perturbation and guide metadata plus PCA scores. This focused object has no UMAP reduction, so no `X_umap` embedding is exported.

```{r packages}
library(Seurat)
library(anndataR)
obj <- readRDS("data/processed/03_k562_perturbation_ready.rds")
stopifnot("gene" %in% colnames(obj[[]]), "sgID_AB" %in% colnames(obj[[]]), "pca" %in% names(obj@reductions))
cat("Seurat cells x genes:", ncol(obj), "x", nrow(obj), "\n")
```

# Write and read H5AD

```{r export}
dir.create("artifacts", showWarnings=FALSE)
out_h5ad <- "artifacts/06_k562_focused_analysis.h5ad"
write_h5ad(obj, out_h5ad, mode="w", assay_name="RNA", x_mapping="data",
           layers_mapping=c(counts="counts"), obs_mapping=TRUE,
           obsm_mapping=list(X_pca="pca"))
cat("Export bytes:", file.info(out_h5ad)$size, "\n")
```

```{r roundtrip-r}
check <- read_h5ad(out_h5ad)
stopifnot(nrow(check$obs)==ncol(obj), nrow(check$var)==nrow(obj))
stopifnot(all(c("gene", "sgID_AB") %in% colnames(check$obs)))
cat("AnnData cells x genes:", paste(dim(check), collapse=" x "), "\n")
cat("Metadata columns:", paste(colnames(check$obs), collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("Embeddings:", paste(names(check$obsm), collapse=", "), "\n")
```

### Interpretation

The R round-trip recovers 3,458 cells, 8,563 genes, perturbation and guide columns, and the PCA embedding. Matching dimensions and metadata support the integrity of the Seurat-to-H5AD export, while deeper numerical equivalence of every assay layer was not tested here.

# Python AnnData and optional Scanpy check

```{r python-config}
reticulate::use_python("C:/Python314/python.exe", required=TRUE)
```

```{python python-check}
import anndata as ad
import importlib.util
import numpy as np
obj_py = ad.read_h5ad("artifacts/06_k562_focused_analysis.h5ad")
source_py = ad.read_h5ad("data/processed/03_k562_powered_sample.h5ad")
assert obj_py.shape == (3458, 8563)
assert {"gene", "sgID_AB"}.issubset(obj_py.obs.columns)
assert "X_pca" in obj_py.obsm
assert obj_py.obsm["X_pca"].shape[0] == obj_py.n_obs
assert obj_py.obs["gene"].astype(str).nunique() == 13
assert obj_py.obs_names.equals(source_py.obs_names)
assert (obj_py.obs["gene"].astype(str) == source_py.obs["gene"].astype(str)).all()
assert "counts" in obj_py.layers
assert (obj_py.layers["counts"] != source_py.X).nnz == 0
assert source_py.var_names.str.replace("_", "-").equals(obj_py.var_names)
renamed_genes = int((source_py.var_names != obj_py.var_names).sum())
print("AnnData:", obj_py.shape, "PCA:", obj_py.obsm["X_pca"].shape)
print("Perturbation classes:", obj_py.obs["gene"].astype(str).nunique())
print("Counts layer matches source; gene names sanitized by Seurat:", renamed_genes)
if importlib.util.find_spec("scanpy"):
    import scanpy as sc
    scanpy_obj = sc.read_h5ad("artifacts/06_k562_focused_analysis.h5ad")
    assert scanpy_obj.shape == obj_py.shape
    assert "X_pca" in scanpy_obj.obsm
    print("Scanpy read verified:", sc.__version__)
else:
    print("Scanpy is not installed; Python AnnData reading and PCA/metadata checks passed.")
```

### Reproducibility note

Python AnnData reads the H5AD and confirms 13 perturbation classes, PCA coordinates, and a counts layer matching the focused source matrix. Seurat changes underscores to hyphens in two duplicate gene names during import; their column positions and counts remain aligned. Scanpy was unavailable in this environment, so Scanpy-specific reading and visualization compatibility were not directly tested.

# Reproducibility manifest

```{r manifest}
paths <- c(list.files("notebooks", pattern="^0[1-6]_.*\\.(Rmd|html)$", full.names=TRUE),
           list.files("results", pattern="\\.csv$", full.names=TRUE),
           list.files("models", pattern="\\.joblib$", full.names=TRUE),
           "data/processed/03_k562_powered_sample.h5ad",
           "data/processed/03_k562_perturbation_ready.rds",
           "data/processed/03_perturbation_effect_matrix.rds",
           "data/processed/04_perturbation_embeddings.rds", out_h5ad)
paths <- unique(paths[file.exists(paths)])
paths <- paths[paths != "notebooks/06_AnnData_Scanpy_interop.html"]
manifest <- data.frame(path=paths, bytes=file.info(paths)$size,
                       md5=unname(tools::md5sum(paths)))
write.csv(manifest, "artifacts/manifest.csv", row.names=FALSE)
capture.output(sessionInfo(), file="artifacts/sessionInfo.txt")
print(manifest[, c("path", "bytes")], row.names=FALSE)
```

### Reproducibility note

The manifest records paths, sizes, and MD5 hashes for selected outputs; `sessionInfo.txt` records the R package environment. The export H5AD and large processed objects remain local, while these records support review of the executed workflow.

## Key results

```{r key-results}
cat("Exported cells:", ncol(obj), "genes:", nrow(obj), "classes:", length(unique(as.character(obj$gene))), "\n")
cat("Manifest entries:", nrow(manifest), "\n")
```

- **Export:** the focused object contains 3,458 cells, 8,563 genes, and 13 perturbation classes in H5AD.
- **Round-trip:** R and Python AnnData checks recover the dimensions, labels, and PCA coordinates.
- **Reproducibility:** 41 manifest entries and R session information identify selected outputs and the execution environment.
